_meta.purpose: Real Gemini 2.5 Flash token counts, captured once so future changes to pixelpath/packing.py or the cost model can be checked against real numbers without spending API calls again.
_meta.tier: free (no billing account) — NOT independently confirmed to tokenize/bill identically to paid tier
_meta.fixed_prompt: Describe this image in one word.
_meta.method: prompt_token_count from response.usage_metadata, minus fixed_prompt_token_count, isolates image-only token cost
_meta.headline_finding: Token cost is FLAT (258) across all tested image dimensions from 100x100 to 3000x4000 — confirmed independently outside the batch script. Gemini 2.5 Flash does NOT scale image token cost with pixel area/tile count in the range tested. This directly contradicts pixelpath/packing.py's current step-function-per-512px-tile model, which was written with an Anthropic-style formula in mind and had never been calibrated against any real provider.
_meta.verdict: packing.py is NOT trustworthy for Gemini as-is. Root cause is understood (wrong cost model shape, not noisy/inconsistent data) but packing.py's logic was deliberately not touched in this probe per the task scope (measurement only).

independent_sanity_check.note: Run outside the batch script to rule out a script artifact, with deliberately extreme sizes

mechanism_investigation.purpose: Narrow down WHY the cost is flat, not just confirm THAT it is

extreme_size_test.note: 10x10 and 32x32 (below the docs' 384px single-tile threshold) and 8000x8000 (would require ~121 tiles at 258 tokens/tile per the documented formula, ~31218 tokens, if tiling applied)
extreme_size_test.conclusion: Flat cost holds across 10x10 to 8000x8000 - not just flat within the originally tested 100x100-3000x4000 range.

content_variation_test.note: Fixed 1000x1000 resolution, blank white vs dense random noise - isolates 'fixed grid regardless of content' from 'content-adaptive quantization'
content_variation_test.conclusion: Identical cost for blank vs dense content at the same resolution - not content-adaptive.

client_side_resize_check.method: Read google-genai SDK source directly (types.py, PIL.Image-to-Part conversion)
client_side_resize_check.finding: value.save(bytes_io, ...) with no resize/thumbnail call - full original-resolution bytes are sent. Client-side resizing ruled out as the cause.

documentation_check.documented_formula: Images <=384px in both dimensions: 258 tokens flat. Larger images: tiled into 768x768 tiles, each costing 258 tokens.
documentation_check.contradiction: The documented formula predicts token cost should scale with size above 384px. Empirical result (flat 258 up to 8000x8000) directly contradicts this.
documentation_check.conclusion: No public documentation found that specifically confirms gemini-2.5-flash overrides the general tiling formula. Mechanism is confirmed by data (robust across 8 orders of magnitude in size and two content extremes) but not fully explained by available public documentation. Plausible unconfirmed explanations: a default media_resolution setting distinct from what the general docs describe, or documentation that has not been updated for 2.5-era models' actual default behavior. Neither is stated as fact.

mechanism_investigation.cross_provider_caveat: This flat-cost behavior is very likely specific to gemini-2.5-flash (possibly its default configuration specifically) and must NOT be assumed to generalize to any other provider without independently re-running this same investigation against it. If a future provider's real cost genuinely does not vary with image size or content, this project's entire region-selection/budget-allocation mechanism may not reduce that provider's real cost at all - a fundamental, provider-dependent limit, not a tuning problem.
